text:
Anya: quick follow-up from the RFC review — we need a concrete plan for slimming the handoff surface between hosted/dedicated/private. proposal: deprecate the heavy sidecar facade and replace with a tiny probe-first shim + capability flags. intent is to reduce translation/duplication and make rollbacks simpler.

Matt: high-level +1. can you outline the failure-mode matrix? my main worry is secrets/rotation and telemetry correlation across probe-only hops.

Anya: agreed. initial thought: the shim only handles 3 things: 1) probe/health+capability negotiation, 2) routing hint propagation (model id, sequence hint), 3) optional auth token passthrough header. it should not massage requests or maintain long-lived state. secret ops (KMS/HSM flow) stays in control plane or the private sidecar when required.

Sasha: caveat: some private deployments rely on the sidecar to inject encryption headers for on-prem HSMs. if we remove that, we need an alternative pattern for private mode (operator-managed sidecar or an init-container) — we can't force customers to change HSM integrations mid-contract.

Jordan: ops perspective: rollout must be staged. suggested phases:
- phase 0: feature-flag probe-first shim in hosted only (no secret change)
- phase 1: enable in dedicated for non-HSM tenants (opt-in)
- phase 2: offer operator-side install for private with migration docs
- phase 3: flip default and deprecate legacy facade after 3mo of no regressions

Anya: that aligns. on telemetry: we must preserve span IDs and request IDs. shim will pass through X-Redwood-Request-Id and x-cloud-trace if present. we also plan a debug header `x-rw-shim-probe` during rollout.

Matt: how do we measure parity? propose a small eval harness: run 1000 synthetic requests/second across 3 typical routes (short chat gen, long-context generation, and embeddings) and compare per-token latency P50/P95, error rate, cost delta. instrumented under both surfaces.

Sasha: add prompt/quality checks too — we must verify no subtle tokenization/encoding changes are introduced (e.g., trimming behavior). Also watch for stream chunk boundaries: streaming edge differences bite customers.

Anya: noted. I'll put together a checklist:
- test harness metrics (latency, p95/p99, token cost)
- streaming chunk parity tests
- request-id/span preservation tests
- secret flow migration docs for HSM tenants
- operator install guide for private mode
- rollout playbook + kill-switch (ff off, fall back to legacy facade)

Jordan: add ops escalation steps and storage of pre-rollout snapshots (configs, metrics baseline). ops-bot: create baseline job?

ops-bot: scheduled: nightly-handoff-baseline-job created (job=handoff-baseline-179999, cadence=daily). link: https://ci.redwood/handoff-baseline-179999

Matt: also check config drift: we need a lint rule that warns if a deployment still references old-facade-only fields. avoid silent failures when the facade is removed.

Anya: good call. I'll add a manifest linter rule and a preflight check in Dedicated provisioning.

Sasha: one more thing — rollback semantics for in-flight KV cache references. If the new shim hands off a request to a runtime that expects a different KV layout, we must have an automatic compatibility probe and soft-fallback to the legacy path. can we gate by runtime capability manifest?

Anya: yes — the handshake includes a capability manifest with KV layout version. shim will verify compatibility and if incompatible will annotate the request and fallback to legacy route. that's part of phase 0 tests.

Matt: timeline idea: RFC -> prototype (2 weeks) -> harness (1 week) -> canary in hosted (2 weeks) -> dedicated opt-ins (3 weeks) -> private operator docs (2 weeks) -> deprecation flip (after 12 weeks of stability).

Jordan: ops ok with that tempo, keep me on the PRs.

Anya: I'll draft a follow-up doc with the matrix and the lint rule details. thanks y'all. :thumbsup: 

ci-bot: PR #4218 opened: "slim-handoff-probe-shim: initial prototype" — https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/4218

Matt: reviewing PR now. please tag me for the harness results.

Sasha: tagging security for HSM docs: @security-team please review proposed operator flow.

Anya: will do. end thread.
